Marshfield, WI 54449-8000  

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Rowan Brooks  
Member ID: W772624569  
Reference number: POC-A5F6D22435-38075  
Requested service: Total hip replacement  
CPT: 27130  
Denial date: August 7, 2026  

Dear Security Health Plan Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement, CPT 27130. The denial states that the imaging findings submitted do not support medical necessity. The clinical record demonstrates that the imaging is consistent with advanced symptomatic hip joint disease and, together with my persistent symptoms, failed conservative treatment, functional limitations, and examination findings, supports the requested procedure.

The June 9, 2026 weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph documented joint-space narrowing to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes. These are objective structural findings of significant degenerative joint disease. The radiograph was weight-bearing and showed marked loss of the affected hip joint space, not merely an incidental or minimal abnormality.

The imaging findings correspond directly with my clinical condition:

- I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- I completed 16 weeks and 16 visits of supervised physical therapy from February 22, 2026, through June 14, 2026, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait.
- I used NSAIDs for six months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on March 29, 2026, produced only three weeks of partial relief.
- I require a cane for ambulation and can walk only one block.
- I cannot put on my shoes without assistance.
- Provocative testing was positive on the affected side, and range of motion was limited by pain.

These records show persistent, function-limiting symptoms despite appropriate nonoperative treatment. The radiographic findings are not being presented in isolation; they are supported by the duration and severity of symptoms, objective examination findings, failed conservative care, and substantial loss of daily function.

The record also does not identify a clinical issue that would make the procedure inappropriate. I have no active infection, no untreated substance-use disorder, a BMI of 29, and I am a nonsmoker. The requested procedure was submitted by Lindqvist, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

Please overturn the denial and authorize total hip replacement, CPT 27130.

The denial notice does not identify the specific medical policy, policy number, version, effective date, clinical-review criteria, or imaging threshold used to reach the determination. The plan has not been quoted in this appeal because the applicable policy text was not provided. Please send me and my surgeon the exact policy and clinical-review criteria applied to this request, including any InterQual or other utilization-management criteria, the specific imaging requirements, and the clinical records relied upon. If the plan believes that the June 9, 2026 radiograph does not satisfy its criteria, please identify precisely which requirement was not met and explain why the documented 1 mm superolateral joint space, subchondral sclerosis, and osteophytes do not support medical necessity in the context of my symptoms and failed treatment.

Please review the complete prior authorization packet, including the radiology report, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, orthopedic examination, and functional limitations. I request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and a written appeal determination.

Sincerely,

[Signature]

Rowan Brooks
